title: How are yall getting your graphics? 🫪
author: punchapath
selftext:
Hey all, just asking a question because I’m generally curious, but how are you guys getting the graphics for your games?

I wanted my game to have a pixel art aesthetic, but the AI I used could not comprehend my color palette and size restrictions, so I ended up making all the graphics myself and just using AI for code.

I’ve been seeing games in this sub though with entire 3d models or even larger pixel art tile sets than mine, so I was just wondering if you guys are also making the graphics yourselves, finding models or textures online, or has AI honestly just gotten that much better since I last tried?

You can check my game out too on r/PunchAPath if you want, the artwork is not my finest but it gets the job done for now haha

replies.author: connected_user93
replies.body:
something like this would need to be touched up manually as it isn't actual pixel art. some of those pixels are deformed and some of them are at inconsistent widths, etc.

there actually are some pretty stellar AI pixel-art generation tools out there but they require customizing open-weight models for the most part.

replies.author: Kalaminator
replies.body: But it is a better start than having nothing, it is not that hard to actually touch this. I could do it, but I wouldn't be able to make a sprite like this from 0.

replies.author: connected_user93
replies.body: I agree, I was more being informational in case OP wants to go down this route

replies.author: punchapath
replies.body:
Yeah I dont think I need pixel perfect artwork, I have kind of just been searching for references online to guide the general shape of my own sprites

This still seems like a great additional resource to find those references, albeit a little more fine tuning would be required

replies.author: MessageSelfdestructs
replies.body: The results from non-dedicated image generators are horrible: inconsistent as hell, and it immediately screams "AI GENERATED" to anyone who sees it.

replies.author: Kalaminator
replies.body: Yeah, it was discussed already. It would be cool to know such dedicated image generators. If people are willing to do some work, you can fix this manually, you can even use software to convert it in real pixel image and then retouch.

replies.author: MessageSelfdestructs
replies.body:
I've trained my own models, but I'm aware that's not really an option for everyone.

But other than that, there's Retro Diffusion, AutoSprite, PixelEngine, PixelLab, etc.  
These models are much better than generating pixel art through ChatGPT/Gemini/Claude, etc.

And if you don't want to pay, there are also open-weights fine-tunes (such as specific Pixel Art LoRAs and XL checkpoints) designed for local Stable Diffusion workflows, but I found the results from those to be a lot less good than the above-mentioned sites.

replies.author: Kalaminator
replies.body:
I only checked pixelEngine and it's super cool, didn't know about these. At the moment I'm not working on pixelated games, but I will pin this somewhere because it is actually super cool if I ever want to go for a pixel game.  
My game is still far from what I would like it to be.

[https://dominion-8adc0.web.app/](https://dominion-8adc0.web.app/)

replies.body: Looking good, but make sure to have a good intro/tutorial for your game if you want people to test/invest time into it.

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body: AI can't do pixel art that well yet. The reason to use it is cheap to make art, which is irrelevant when you use AI.

replies.author: punchapath
replies.body: Yeah, I’m not saying my specific project had a great use case for AI graphics, I was just more or less surprised how a lot of models can generate high res textures and models with ease but continue to struggle with something much smaller like pixel art

replies.author: kytheon
replies.body:
"something much smaller like pixel art"  
  
Think about what pixel art is. Limited color palette, needs to convey meaning with way less pixels. Consistency is even more important, because every pixel counts. And most of all, if you ask a random AI to generate pixel art, it creates something that is similar but isn't pixel art. Because it'll usually have the pixels not even aligned. Like a 4K image of a small pixel character, but with the pixels not on a grid. Each pixel is represented by a whole bunch of pixels. Etc.

Just because pixel art is simpler and smaller, doesn't make it easier. Learn what pixel art is, and you'll realize you shouldn't use it for your AI game at all.

replies.author: MessageSelfdestructs
replies.body:
"*Learn what pixel art is, and you'll realize you shouldn't use it for your AI game at all.*"

Your advice seems to be based on... yeah, what is it based on?

I'd ignore you if I were the OP, as you don't seem to be knowledgeable about this. At all.

replies.author: MessageSelfdestructs
replies.body:
That's just not true.

There's quite a few models that are dedicated to pixel art, and they give very nice results.  
Not always flawless, and definitely need some touching up here and there, but to state that AI can't do well only makes it look as if you generated it through LLMs, instead of dedicated pixel art models...

comments.author: vurt72
comments.body: My own fine tune, on my own stuff actually. Though it's in a sort of feed-back loop, it's now trained on its own outputs quite a lot, being super selective for that though. I use SDXL.  UI use FLOW (google) to animate.. i have my own tools for extracting frames, doing transparency etc.
